payload.report: Echocardiography demonstrates a quadricuspid aortic valve with four equal cusps causing severe outflow obstruction (peak gradient 131.1 mm Hg), severe left ventricular hypertrophy, and an apical aneurysm. This congenital structural lesion explains the murmur present since age 3, the loud 4/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border, and the long benign clinical course. An innocent/functional murmur is ruled out by the organic valve lesion. Acromegalic features are present but appeared later and are at most a secondary modifying condition, not the primary cause. The apical aneurysm is best understood as a complication of chronic severe outflow obstruction. Thus the primary diagnosis is congenital quadricuspid aortic stenosis.
